name: Stanley Lake Creek Dispersed Camping - Sawtooth National Forest

management_agency.name: U.S. Forest Service - Sawtooth National Recreation Area (SNRA)

rules_and_regulations.cost: 100% Free - No fees, no permits required for dispersed primitive camping
rules_and_regulations.stay_limit: 16 consecutive days max stay limit within Sawtooth NRA
rules_and_regulations.guidelines: Dispersed primitive camping permitted at designated campsites marked with camp posts along Stanley Lake Creek road corridor. Camping set back 100ft from water.

waste_disposal_rules.poop_disposal: Cathole method: dig 6 inches deep into granitic mountain soil, 200 feet from streams and lakes. Pack out all toilet paper.
waste_disposal_rules.trash_policy: Strict Leave No Trace. Black bear country: hard-sided vehicle or bear canister food storage mandatory.

campfire_rules.firewood_policy: Gather dead and downed wood only.
campfire_rules.safety_requirements: Campfires permitted in designated stone/metal fire rings only. Extinguish cold to touch with creek water.

access_and_road_conditions.road_conditions: Washboard gravel road with small rocks and shallow dips.

nomad_connectivity_rating.verizon_reliability: 2-3 bars 4G LTE (10-25 Mbps download near ID-21 junction)
nomad_connectivity_rating.terrain_obstruction_risk: Moderate (Towering Sawtooth Mountain peaks create signal shadows in deep glens)

amenities: Panoramic Views of Sawtooth Mountain Spires

services_available: St. Luke's Wood River Medical Center

seasonal_weather_effects.spring: Late May thaw: cold (35-50°F), high snowmelt runoff, lingering snowpacks.

seasonal_weather_effects.fall: Golden aspen leaf season (50-65°F daytime, sub-freezing 20-30°F nights), low humidity.
seasonal_weather_effects.winter: Severe alpine winter (-15 to 25°F), heavy snow, FS 640 snow-covered and closed to cars.

High altitude solar exposure and dehydration
Freezing night temperatures even in summer months

human_demographics_and_culture: Sawtooth Wilderness backpackers, fly anglers, digital nomads, mountain bikers, and alpine photographers.
